text: Historical sources explain that the colonization of the Mosfell region started soon after the beginning of the settlement of Iceland around AD 870. The Mosfell area was part of the land claim of the first settler of Iceland, Ingolf Arnarson, who established his farm in modern-day Reykjavik. According to the written sources, Skeggjastaðir, south of the Leirvog River, is supposed to have been the first farm established in the Mosfell region. The Book of Settlements* states: There was a man named Thord the Bearded. He was the son of Hrapp who was the son of Björn Buna. Thord went to Iceland and took land with the permission of Ingolf within his initial land-claim between the Ulfar and Leirvog rivers. Landnámabók (The Book of Settlements) This passage states that Ingolf granted Thord the Bearded the land on which he founded his farm at Skeggjastaðir. Based on our knowledge of the conditions during the settlement of Iceland, this passage also suggests that these two men were friends.
